writerNotes: route: the hero walks a client's programme across a map. Write the start label, three short goals a client of this coach would set (the last is the summit), the sessions and weeks of the main programme, and a flag colour that suits the brand.

log: the four labels beside the map and the word before the week number. stages: six steps of working with this coach, in their voice: where you are, the summit, the route, the sessions, the hard part, the top.
programmes: the brief's programmes exactly (prices, sessions, length, what's included), each with a line on why someone would choose it; badge the one most people pick, or -1 for none.
fit.qs: two to five short questions a prospective client could answer honestly, each answer scoring every programme 0 to 3 so the highest total points to the right one.
coach: the coach's real name, background and only the credentials the brief gives (never invent qualifications or results); their initials for the monogram.
No testimonials or outcome claims beyond the brief. The call booking really sends: the request goes to the coach, who confirm it. Never say it is booked, paid or confirmed.

hero.title and hero.titleEm: a short two-part headline (four lines at most on a desktop; the second part is set in italics); section titles have a second half. theme.accent is the coach's colour, deep enough for white button text; theme.wordmarkFit is always "fit".
business.name is set to exactly the name in the brief and cannot be changed; brand.name is how it appears in the nav and the footer (short).
